servinfo.title: Front Suspension Frame, Stabilizer Bar and Bushing Removal and Installation

ptxt.intxrefpoff: Front Suspension Frame and Stabilizer Bar Components

item.ptxt: If the front suspension frame is not stably supported on a transmission jack or other supporting equipment during its removal and installation, the frame could drop and cause personal injury.
Check that the weight of the front suspension frame is supported at the frame’s center and that the frame is well balanced on the support.
Touching a hot exhaust system component will cause a burn.
Do not perform any service work on the exhaust system until the exhaust system is cool.
The front suspension frame bolt (long one) and steering gear case bolt are pre-coated with friction stabilizer. If these bolts are reused, they may work loose.
Never reuse the front suspension frame bolt (long one) and steering gear case bolt.
If steering gear cover is reused, it will lose the sealing performance and water may enter the gearbox.
Do not reuse the steering gear cover.

s1.ptxt: Disconnect steering lower shaft from pinion shaft.
Hoist vehicle and remove front wheels.
Remove engine undercover and engine under side covers.
Disconnect muffler mounting No.1 from front suspension frame.
Disconnect stabilizer joint from stabilizer bar.
Disconnect tie-rod end from steering knuckle.
Remove suspension arm.
Remove engine rear torque rod bolt from bracket.
Support front suspension frame (2) using transmission jack (1).

Remove front suspension frame bolts (1) and front suspension frame rear bolts (2), and then lower transmission jack to remove suspension frame (3) together with stabilizer bar, torque rod, torque rod cover and steering gear case from vehicle body.
Remove steering gear case assembly from front suspension frame.
Remove torque rod cover from front suspension frame.
Remove engine rear torque rod from front suspension frame.
Remove stabilizer mounting bracket (1), stabilizer bar bushing (2) and stabilizer bar (3) from front suspension frame (4).

ptxt.intxrefpoff: Front Stabilizer Bar, Bushing and Joint Check

s1.ptxt: Install front stabilizer bar (1), bushings (2) and mounting brackets (3) to front suspension frame as follows.

s2.ptxt: Position stabilizer bar with identification painting (5) facing up at right side.
Position stabilizer bar bushing with its slit (6) facing forward and its end closely fit against ring (4) of stabilizer bar.
Tighten stabilizer bar mounting bracket bolts (7) temporarily, and then tighten them to specified torque.

s1.ptxt: Install engine rear torque rod to front suspension frame.
Install torque rod cover (1) to front suspension frame (2) as shown in figure.
Install steering gear case assembly to front suspension frame.
Install suspension arm to front suspension frame, and then tighten new suspension arm front bushing bolts temporarily by hand.
Put front suspension frame (2) on transmission jack (1) and raise jack.
Fix front suspension frame with bolts as follows.

s2.ptxt: Tighten new front suspension frame bolt (1) temporarily.
Tighten new front suspension frame bolt (2) to specified torque.
Tighten front suspension frame bolts (1), (3) and front suspension frame rear bolts (4) to specified torque.

s1.ptxt: Lower transmission jack.
Install engine rear torque rod bolt and tighten it to specified torque.
Connect suspension arm joint to steering knuckle.
Connect tie-rod end to steering knuckle.
Connect stabilizer joint to stabilizer bar.
Install muffler mounting No.1 to front suspension frame.
Install front wheels and tighten wheel nuts to specified torque.
Connect steering lower shaft to pinion shaft.
Lower hoist and bounce vehicle up and down several times to stabilize suspension. And then, tighten suspension arm front bushing bolts to specified torque.
Install engine undercover and engine under side covers.
Check front wheel alignment.
